question.text: What is KYC/AML in the context of mutual fund regulations?

answer.text: A mutual fund performance measurement tool
Know Your Customer / Anti-Money Laundering - processes to verify investor identity and prevent illegal use of financial systems
A type of mutual fund scheme

explanation.text: The Logic: KYC (Know Your Customer) and AML (Anti-Money Laundering) requirements verify the investor's identity and address under PMLA/AML laws. AML compliance is particularly relevant to cash transactions, and intermediaries are required to maintain AML/CFT documentation as part of the prescribed framework. The Trap: KYC/AML is a compliance requirement, not a performance measurement, a scheme type, or a tax computation method. All investors, regardless of amount invested, must complete KYC. Note: Helping investors understand that these checks protect the integrity of the financial system can ease onboarding, especially for first-time or retired investors.
